target_customer: K-12 school districts (free) and learning application developers (who pay for access)
problem: Teachers and IT staff spent hours creating accounts and logging students into each learning app.
business_model: Two sided: free single sign-on and rostering for districts, paid integrations for app developers
product_category: Education identity, single sign-on and rostering platform

founders.name: Dan Carroll
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and product lead per YC page.

founders.name: Rafael Garcia
founders.background_notes: Later co-founder and CTO of Kernel, a browser infrastructure company.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with many school information systems and learning apps via an API and later single sign-on was standard engineering with heavy integration breadth.

defensibility.rationale: Once a district's rosters and a developer's integration run through Clever, replacement is costly, and each added app and district made the platform more useful.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge; Clever stayed independent until Kahoot! bought it in 2021.

market_need_then: Schools were adopting many apps and teachers lost class time to manual logins and account setup, and developers faced a costly district by district integration problem.

branding.domain_note: Uses clever.com; no purchase story found.

identity.logo: Wordmark whose mark is the first letter; 2023 guidelines specify the Euclid Circular B font
identity.visual_style: Clean modern layout, shape patterns, icons and real classroom photography
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, reassuring and mission driven: 'Connecting every student to a world of learning.'

branding.brand_signature: The Clever Badge, a QR code card young students flash to log in
branding.community_and_virality: NPR reported in 2015 that a third of schools used the app most people had never heard of, so adoption ran ahead of public brand awareness.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly name and a tangible Badge product helped teachers and kids, though the brand was known mainly inside schools.

outcome_analysis: Clever started with an API to provision student accounts, won early attention in 2013, raised $10.3M in 2014 from Sequoia and $30M from Lightspeed, then added free single sign-on for districts. Giving districts the product free while charging app developers drove rapid adoption, reaching around half of US K-12 schools, and Kahoot! bought it for up to $500M in 2021.
notes: Deal value is up to $500M per Kahoot! and press, with an enterprise value range of $435M to $500M reported depending on milestones. A seed of about $3M in October 2012 appears only on aggregators and is unverified, so it is not a round. Total raised of about $43M comes from press after the Series B; later financing, if any, was not found. YC page lists only Carroll and Garcia as founders; the CEO is not named in the sources fetched. Dated competitor search found nothing from 2012; ClassLink and Edlink appear only in undated later blog posts, so the list is empty. Company claimed 2020 revenue of about $44M per one report.
